context: Transient incompressible flow: two-dimensional turbulent flow over a backward-facing step with a contraction (pitzDaily), unsteady RANS with the k-epsilon model, inlet velocity 10 m/s, started from rest. Solved with OpenFOAM pimpleFoam (PIMPLE algorithm) with a fixed, deliberately large time step (Courant number well above one), so every time step needs several under-relaxed outer pressure-velocity iterations; the outer loop of a step ends when the initial residuals of all equations are below their tolerances, or at a cap of 50 outer iterations. Goal: finish the run with as few outer iterations per time step as possible while every step still meets its tolerances. The momentum (U) under-relaxation factor of the outer iterations acts like a pseudo time step within the time step: larger values (less under-relaxation) give faster convergence of the outer loop up to a stability limit, beyond which the outer loop converges more slowly, erratically or not at all. The pressure factor is set automatically from the momentum factor; only the momentum factor is decided.
